simple.meaning: שַׁחַד (shachad) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a donation (venal or redemptive).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 23 times across Exodus, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, and 7 more, beginning at Exodus 23:8. Its contexts include family, family line, righteousness, kingship, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שַׁחַד (H7810).

definitions.full: H7810. shochad שֹׁ֫חַד noun masculine present , specifically bribe ; — ׳שׁ absolute Isa 1:23 22 t.; — bribe , usually to pervert justice, object of לָקַח Exod 23:8 a (E), = Deut 16:19 a, 10:17 ; 1Sam 8:3 ; 2Chr 19:7 ; Psa 15:5 ; Prov 17:23 ; + infinitive, take bribe to do something, Deut 27:25 ; Ezek 22:12 ; שׁ ׳אָהַב Isa 1:23 ; compare also 5:23 ; 33:15 ; Exod 23:8 b (E) = Deut 16:19 b, Micah 3:11 ; Psa 26:10 ; Prov 17:8 ; 21:14 ; ׳אָהֳלֵישֿׁ Job 15:34 , i.e. abode of bribe-givers; ׳שׁ Prov 6:35 (|| כֹּפֶר ) is hush-money, or (possibly) legal compensation (compare Toy); ׳שׁ elsewhere (with שָׁהַ ) of bribing king to take sides 1Kin 15:19 ; 2Kin 16:8 , compare Isa 45:13 (|| מְחִיר ).
